fgApp: foreground app — the panel detects which one
searchDenied: Couldn’t open the search for typing
searchNoReturn: Couldn’t get back to the previous app: nothing was sent
suggest: has no profile. Create one with ready-made shortcuts?
name: Name
voiceHint: This name is also what you say out loud: “click …”.
recording: Press the combo on your keyboard…
dupHint: Keep it in one place so you don’t see it twice.
pickOne: Pick a shortcut to edit it.
dTap: Presses and releases the combo, like a keyboard.
dHold: Keeps keys pressed while your finger is on the button. Great for push-to-talk.
dToggle: One tap presses, another releases. Hold a key without holding your finger.
dMacro: Runs several steps with a single tap.
dUrl: Opens a web page in your browser.
dApp: Opens a program, file or command.
tplSub: Pick an app, or describe any other and AI will prepare its shortcuts.
autoSuggest: When I open an app without a profile, suggest creating one.
pvEmpty: Tap a template to preview its shortcuts before installing.
touchSub: Tune how forgiving the panel is with imprecise taps. Applies to all profiles.
sDebD: A second tap on the same button within this time is ignored. Other buttons are never blocked.
sHitD: A tap landing near a button (in the gap) still triggers it.
sMovD: If your finger moves more than this, the tap doesn’t count.
testIdle: Tap several times in a row to see what gets filtered.
relSub: Your panel always there, like an assistive device.
rStartD: The panel appears when you turn on the computer.
rAutoD: Saves a copy whenever you change something (last 12).
rCrashD: If something fails, the last good copy is restored.
rSingleD: Opening it again just shows the existing panel.
ob0b: A floating panel with big buttons to copy, dictate, switch windows and more — no hunting for keys.
ob1t: How do you use your computer?
ob1b: We’ll tune size and touch precision for you. Pick as many as apply.
ob2t: Which apps do you use most?
ob2b: We’ll install their shortcuts. The panel switches on its own when you open each one.
kitBasicsD: Copy, paste, undo, dictate and more, in any app
ready: Ready. Tap a button to use it.
editHint: Tap a button to edit it or × to remove it
safeMaxD: Applies to Hold, Toggle and Sticky keys. Each shortcut can have its own time.
safeSwitchD: Keeps a held Ctrl from affecting the next program.
reduceMD: Removes animations and transitions. Also follows the Windows setting.
resetFreqD: Clears usage history and shortcuts pinned to Frequent.
aiPrivacy: Only the program name and language are sent. Nothing from your documents.
consentD: To create shortcuts, the program name and your keyboard language are sent to an external service. Nothing else. You can turn it off anytime.
errOffD: Couldn’t reach the service. Check your internet or use another option.
errLimD: You used today’s 5 free generations. They renew tomorrow, or use your own key.
errAiOffD: You chose not to use AI. Turn it on or continue with templates and empty profiles.
onlyEs: Template reviewed only in Spanish: check the keys.
shareHint: To share one, open it in Shortcuts and tap ✏ → Share.
importedPv: Profile imported: review it and choose what to install
compatD: For games and apps that ignore shortcuts: sends physical keys. Some anti-cheats may block it.
rollbackD: Available 7 days after updating. Your profiles are kept.
rolledBack: Will go back to the previous version on restart (simulated)
obVt: How do you want the panel?
obVb: You can change it anytime in Quick settings.
rAdminD: Needed to send shortcuts to programs running as administrator.
blockedB: Windows won’t let an app send this combo (it’s reserved for the system). The button won’t do anything.
blockedS: Windows treats it specially: it may behave differently than on the keyboard. Test it before relying on it.
autoReleaseD: For safety, if you forget it held it releases by itself. It also releases when you switch apps.
vh1: Turn on Windows voice access with Win + Ctrl + S, or say “Voice access, wake up”.
vh2: With the panel visible, say “click {index}” or “click {name}”.
vh3: Turn on “Numbers for voice” in Quick settings to see the number on each button.
badUrl: This address doesn’t look valid (e.g. example.com)
tagline: Whatever you want to do, clícalo.
actionUnavailable: This action is not available yet
processTaken: {process} already opens “{profile}”. Move it to this profile?
itemGone: It no longer exists: it may have been deleted.
generalFixed: General can’t be deleted or linked to an app.
backupDamaged: This backup is damaged and wasn’t restored.
engineFault: Something failed; the keys were released
incompleteTap: This shortcut is incomplete · Tap ✏ to complete it
keyMissing: {key} is not on the keyboard layout of {app}
releasedOnLock: Keys were released when the computer was locked or suspended
launchUnsafe: For safety, Clícalo doesn’t open this: {name}
guardianUnstable: Key protection is off · Restart Clícalo to bring it back
saveFailD: Retrying every 30 s. Your changes are still here.
saveReadOnly: Read-only: your data comes from a newer version of Clícalo
dataUnreadable: Your data could not be read. It was set aside, not deleted; accept the new panel to save it.
textUnavailable: Text not available · type it again
schemaNewer: This copy is from a newer version and is not applied
importInvalid: The file is not a valid Clícalo copy
importTooLarge: The file is too large to import
releasedSwitch: You switched apps: held keys were released
releasedAuto: Released automatically after {count} s for safety
adminMsg: {app} runs as administrator. Windows won’t let Clícalo send shortcuts to it unless Clícalo is too.
emptyProfT: This profile has no shortcuts yet
co1d: Fold the bar or open it as the full panel.
co2d: ★ shows Frequent; the other button, your profile. Auto/Fixed decides if it follows the app.
co3d: Search, repeat, pinned shortcuts, auto-fold and page scrolling.
tmStart: Test mode: tap buttons to see if the touch counts. Nothing is sent.
phTouch: You touch the button: keys are pressed…
phHolding: They stay pressed while your finger stays
phLatched: They stay pressed even after you lift
twTap: Presses these keys together and releases them, like a keyboard.
twHold: Keeps them pressed while your finger is on the button.
twToggle: 1st tap: keeps them pressed. 2nd tap: releases.
twText: Types this text where the cursor is.
twUrl: Opens this page in your browser.
twMouse: Performs this mouse action where the pointer is.
testHow: The control center hides, the chosen app is activated, the shortcut is sent and you come back here.
testAskQ: Did it do what you expected in {app}?
tip1: Program language changes keys (Bold: Ctrl+N in Spanish, Ctrl+B in English).
tip2: Check the keyboard layout in Templates → Keyboard.
tip3: Some programs need a specific side of Ctrl or Alt: try the Left / Right tab.
tip4: If the app is slow to respond, make it a macro with a wait.
genLinkS: Used in any app without its own profile.
waitingS: Open or switch to the program you want to link. We’ll recognize it.
unlinkedS: Not linked to any app. Pick one so it switches automatically.
linkDetect: Capture the next app I use
waitingApp: Open the app you want to link…
blankSub: Start with no shortcuts and add your own, for any program or task.
unknownMsg: I couldn’t find reliable shortcuts for “{app}”. Here are common shortcuts that usually work, but check them.
replaceMsg: Replacing {keys}. Tap the new keys; changes save automatically.
pinAllOff2: Now it only shows when you use “{profile}”. Turn on to always see it in the fixed row at the top of the panel.
pinAllOn2: Always visible in any app, in the fixed row at the top of the panel.
testSafe: Nothing is sent from here, so your work isn’t affected.
testWhat: Tapping it on the panel will send {keys} to {app}.
createOwnD: Give it a name, choose what it does, done.
iconAuto: Icon picked from the name · tap the icon to change it
iconManual: Icon picked by you · tap the icon to change it
comboEmpty: Tap keys in the order they are pressed. E.g.: Ctrl, then C.
orderHint2: Pressed in the order you tap them. Tap a chosen key to remove it.
pinAllOff: Now it only shows in “{profile}”. Turn on to move it to the “Always visible” row in every app.
pinAllOn: It’s in the “Always visible” row: shows in every app. Turn off to return it to one profile.
dupAdvG: It’s already in “Always visible”, so the rest are redundant: it shows twice on the panel.
dupAdvSame: Same name and combo in several profiles. You can keep it once in “Always visible”.
dupAdvDiff: Different actions sharing a combo. Usually fine (each app interprets it its own way).
dupKept: Marked as intentional. You won’t be warned again.
dupChangeT: Combo cleared: tap the new keys below
tplSub2: Create profiles with AI or install proven templates. Everything adapts to your keyboard.
aiHeroD: Type or dictate its name. AI proposes the most useful shortcuts and you choose which to keep.
kbWhy: Detected from Windows. Combos change with language (Bold is Ctrl+N in Spanish, Ctrl+B in English).
noSugOn: No open apps without a profile. We’ll let you know when you open one.
noSugOff: Detection is off. Turn it on so the panel offers profiles for new apps.
allInstalled: You installed every template. Use AI for any other program.
instNoteAll: Already installed with all these shortcuts.
instNoteSome_one: Installed. {count} shortcut from this template is missing.
instNoteSome_other: Installed. {count} shortcuts from this template are missing.
pinOnA: The bar stays open. Tap so it folds itself.
pinOffA: The bar folds after using a button. Tap to keep it open.
asDesc: When you open a program without a profile, the panel offers to create one in a tap.
activeLegend: The dot marks the active app
dDockD: Tucks into the screen edge and opens with one tap.
followAppD: Same as the panel’s 🔄 / 🔒 button: blue follows the active app, red keeps it fixed. Frequent never switches.
aboutSub: Why this tool exists and how to reach me.
dFullD: Everything visible: fixed row, tabs, keys and notices.
dCompactD: No tabs or keys; pick the profile at the top. About half the size.
dStripD: A single row of buttons you can place anywhere.
mFreqD: Your most-used shortcuts, in any app.
mFixedD: Stays even when you switch programs.
sysSub: Updates, backups and startup, in one place.
aiSub: Type or dictate the name of any program.
seeWelcomeD: Replay the setup: how you use your computer, your apps and the look.
rowsVisD: Fewer rows = smaller panel. Remaining buttons move to other pages.
showStripD: Hide it for a shorter panel; those buttons stay in the edge tab.
showTabsD: The row with ★ Frequent and your profile. If hidden, the profile still follows the active app.
dockCount: Buttons per page in the bar
updSub: Improvements without losing your shortcuts: profiles are saved before updating.
updAutoD: Installs itself while you’re not using the panel.
updAskD: Shows a notice and you pick the moment.
updBackupD: Creates a backup of your profiles.
channelD: Beta gets new features first, with possible bugs.
fbSub: Your experience improves the tool for everyone. Write to me directly.
fbType: What would you like to tell me?
fbPh: Tell me in your own words… you can dictate with the mic.
fbLogD: Includes macro_quick_access.log to find the bug.
fbSysD: App and Windows version. Nothing personal.
fbSendD: Your email app opens with the message ready.
creator: Creator of Macro Quick Access
fbPromise: I read every message. If you describe how you use your computer, I can adapt the tool to you.
fbGhD: Opens a public issue in the repository.
story1: I built this tool after a spinal cord injury. I only use the touchscreen because I can’t move my fingers, and I needed to do with one tap what others do with a keyboard.
story2: I share it so more people with reduced mobility can use their computer faster and more independently. If it helps even one more person, it was worth it.
shareD: Know someone it could help? Share it.
ccSub: Shortcuts, templates, columns, language and more
lockA: Fixed (red): profile won’t switch with the app. Tap to go back to Auto.
autoA: Auto (blue): follows the active app. Tap to fix the current profile.
modOnce: will be added to your next tap or click
handlePosD: You can also drag it along the edge.
voiceOff: Turn on “Numbers for voice” in Quick settings to see this number on the panel.
autoDimD: After a few seconds it turns almost transparent; touch it to bring it back.
panelSub: Language, look and how the panel behaves so it never covers your work.
barExplain: The panel tucks into a slim tab on the screen edge. Tap it to open the bar: it closes itself after you use a button and never covers the scrollbar.
autoHideD: The bar tucks away and frees the screen.
gutterD: Leaves the edge clear so you can scroll in Word or the browser.
fbSoundD: A short click confirms the shortcut was sent.
fbFlashD: The button lights up briefly when triggered.
globalSub: Shows in every app. Great for dictation and voice.
orderHint: This is how they look on the panel. Tap one to edit; change its position with the buttons, no dragging.
libHint: Tap an action to add it to “{profile}”. No typing needed.
dictNameT: Dictation on (Win + H): say the button name
recHint: Optional, if someone has a keyboard handy.
dText: Types saved text —your email, signature or address— without a keyboard.
dMouse: Performs a mouse action: right click, double click, drag or scroll.
textHint: You can dictate it with the mic button.
